thread:
nina: Heads-up: we just saw a sharp tail-latency increase in eu-central dedicated pools around 14:03 UTC. Correlates with NIC TX drops and a spike in short-lived outbound TLS sessions from tenant `hummingbird`.
omar: noticed that too. pcap shows tons of SYN/FIN pairs to kv-internal-eu1 on :443, very high churn.
lee: ops-bot flagged: net-drop-euc-14:03 - tx_errors on rack-7 nic0 (rx_ok, tx_errs up 12k).
ops-bot: ALERT: net-drop-euc-14:03 - NIC_TX_ERRORS rack-7:nic0 > 1000 in 1m.
sam: Could be a head-of-line on NIC queue due to many small TLS sessions. Noisy tenant creating ~30k new connections/minute -> kernel and hw queue thrash.
nina: Quick mitigation option: move hummingbird to dedicated-pool-iso-1 (isolated rack) and throttle its new_conn_rate via BPF shaper on its node's egress. Pros/cons?
omar: moving to isolated rack buys isolation but requires free capacity. If we evict other tenants we pay in latency/cost. BPF shaper is low-latency and per-tenant; we have a prototype in eng-infra/patches but not prod-approved.
lee: We can also flip a routing rule to route hummingbird egress through nat-gw-dedicated-1 that we use for Dedicated tenants. That reduces SNAT churn on shared gw and gives temporary headroom.
nina: Ops: can we apply BPF shaper as emergency to specific POD IPs? We need a quick ACL mapping tenant->IP list.
infra-oncall: oncall here. I can apply a fail-safe BPF filter (allow X new connections/s per source IP) for 30m. Will require a small ipset of hummingbird pod CIDRs. Requesting +1.
sam: +1. Add a fail-open: if BPF hits >95% packet drop, auto-remove after 2m to avoid collateral.
ops-bot: ACTION_CREATED: change-request #4982 - apply per-tenant egress_bpf_shaper for tenant hummingbird; move to nat-gw-dedicated-1 fallback. Created by infra-oncall.
billing: ping on cost impact: moving tenant to nat-gw-dedicated-1 will increase their bill (dedicated egress costs) but reduce shared infra footprint. Also turning on BPF shaper has negligible cost.
lee: Rolling change: 1) add hummingbird to ipset on nodes in rack-7; 2) apply tc-bpf egress program with token-bucket of 1500 new_conn/s per pod. 3) reroute their pool to nat-gw-dedicated-1. Canary on single node first.
omar: Snippet for BPF config we used in canary: 
```
# tc-bpf pseudo
map new_conn_counters
rule: if SYN && conn not tracked -> inc counter(src_ip) if counter(src_ip) > burst_limit -> drop
```
sam: Also will instrument metrics: per-tenant new_conn_rate, per-node nic_tx_err_rate, and per-nat-gw snat_ports_in_use. Set alert at 70%/25k new_conn/min.
ops-bot: NOTE: deploy-bot will stamp changes; remember to include rollback: remove ipset + unload bpf.
infra-oncall: Applying canary now to rack-7/node-21. Monitoring CPU and NIC drops.
ops-bot: UPDATE: canary applied. node-21 nic_tx_err down 82%, P95 tail latency for small gens down from 610ms -> 48ms.
billing: initial estimate: if hummingbird stays on dedicated nat-gw for 30d, delta ~+$3.6k/mo. If they fix SDK to reuse HTTP/2 channels, recouped quickly.
lee: Product/SE action: please contact hummingbird engineering and ask them to enable connection pooling or SDK keepalive v2. I'll draft a template.
omar: Follow-ups: 1) harden BPF shaper for prod (tests + safety hooks) 2) add per-tenant connection pooling guidance + SDK changes 3) evaluate cheaper per-node multiplexer vs whole dedicated nat-gw 4) add runbook for NIC-level noisy-tenant detection.
sam: Long-term idea: route high-churn tenants via TLS-terminating outbound proxy that multiplexes upstream (reduces 4-tuple churn). Tradeoff: infra + TLS termination CPU. Need perf numbers.
ops-bot: RESOLVED: net-drop-euc-14:03 - egress shaping + routing change reduced NIC errors and tail latencies. Monitoring 60m.
infra-oncall: Will file postmortem stub and follow the checklist. If any node.nic_tx_err > 900 for >5m, auto-escalate.
lee: Thanks team. I pushed a short runbook note in release-war-room: "apply-bpf-tenant-shaper" with command snippets and rollback guidance.
nina: Closing loop: ensure billing notifies tenant of increased egress cost and we track SDK fix adoption.
